name: Ansible TLS certificate verification disabled
attack_scenario: an on-path attacker (rogue Wi-Fi, ARP/DNS spoofing, compromised proxy) presents a self-signed cert, and Ansible fetches the attacker's payload or leaks basic-auth credentials because it never checks the certificate chain
negative_test_hint: set "validate_certs: no" on the download task and assert the playbook keeps certificate verification enabled instead

exemplar.noncompliant:
- ansible.builtin.get_url:
      url: https://repo.example.com/pkg.tar.gz
      dest: /tmp/pkg.tar.gz
      validate_certs: no
exemplar.compliant:
- ansible.builtin.get_url:
      url: https://repo.example.com/pkg.tar.gz
      dest: /tmp/pkg.tar.gz
      validate_certs: yes
exemplar.explanation: validate_certs: no turns off TLS certificate verification in get_url/uri and every HTTP-based module, so the connection is encrypted but unauthenticated and an on-path attacker can swap in a malicious payload or steal basic-auth credentials. Verification defaults to yes and should stay on; disabling it is almost always insecure.
